turns.text: Hi, this is Sara calling from the clinic about your recent knee surgery. Am I speaking with Vivian?
Yes, this is Vivian.
Thanks, Vivian. To confirm your identity, can you tell me your date of birth?
March third, nineteen fifty-eight.
Thank you. Are you having any pain today?
Yes, some.
On a scale from zero to ten, how bad is it?
About a five. It's a tight, aching feeling in my calf, below the new knee.
Is it better, worse, or about the same as yesterday?
About the same.
Have you had a fever, a temperature over one hundred point four, since you went home?
No.
How does your incision look? Any redness, drainage, or opening?
It looks fine.
Is either of your legs swollen?
Just the left leg. The calf is puffier than yesterday, and it's tender.
Thank you for telling me. Swelling in one calf is something a nurse should look at today, so I'm flagging it now. Are you sleeping well?
Pretty well, yes.
And overall, how are you feeling?
Okay.
Do you have any questions for your care team?
No, I don't think so.
A nurse will call you back today about the swelling. If you get chest pain or trouble breathing, call nine one one right away. Take care, Vivian.
Okay. Thank you. Bye.
